title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 31-33). This is the proof of a factorization lemma in Grothendieck's c. 1965-71 notes on algebraic cycles over an algebraically closed field k. The objects are:
- X and Y smooth projective varieties, with A_Y = Alb(Y).
- S_Y : A_0(Y)_{deg 0} -> A_Y(k), the summation (Albanese) map. Its kernel defines Albanese equivalence on 0-cycles, so A_{0,alb}(Y) is identified with A_Y(k).
- Z, a correspondence (cycle on Y x X) inducing u_Z : A_{0,alb}(Y) = A_Y(k) -> A^i_alb(X). The target is codimension-i cycles algebraically equivalent to 0, modulo Albanese equivalence.

The statement on p. 31: there exist a homomorphism phi : A' -> A_Y of abelian varieties and Z' in A^i_alg(X x A') with Z'(0)=0, so that a' |-> Z'(a') is a group homomorphism, and u_Z o phi = v_{Z'}. In words, the cycle classes reached by Z are parametrized by an abelian variety through a homomorphic algebraic family.

The proof on p. 31 starts from a hypothetical universal family: a cycle U on Y x A_Y with S_Y(U(a)) = a. With it one would set Z'(a) = Z(U(a)) and get Z(v) = Z'(S(v)). Such a U need not exist.

This page.
1. One cannot always find U with S_Y(U(a)) = a, but one can find U with S_Y(U(a)) = n a for some n >= 1. (Implicitly: take a curve C in Y with J(C) -> Alb(Y) surjective, choose a quasi-section A_Y -> J(C) by Poincaré reducibility, and pull back a Poincaré/Abel-Jacobi family of divisors on C.)
2. Put Z'(a) := Z(U(a)). Claim: Z'(S_Y(N)) = n Z(N) for every 0-cycle N of degree 0 on Y.
3. Proof. Let a = S_Y(N). Then S_Y(U(a)) = n a = S_Y(nN), so U(a) = nN in A_{0,alb}(Y). Hence Z(U(a)) = n Z(N), i.e. Z'(a) = n Z(N).
4. The same identity applied to N = U(a) gives Z'(S_Y(U(a))) = n Z(U(a)), i.e. Z'(na) = n Z'(a). So Z' is compatible with multiplication by n.
5. A first attempt, crossed out, produced the spurious n^2 Z(N).
6. Eliminating n. Since A_Y(k), equivalently A_{0,alb}(Y), is divisible, write N = nL. Applying the above to L gives Z'(S_Y(L)) = n Z(L) = Z(N). So every class Z(N) is of the form Z'(b) with b in A_Y(k).
7. Equivalently, in the formulation of p. 31: take A' = A_Y, phi = multiplication by n, and Z'(a) = Z(U(a)). Then u_Z o phi = v_{Z'}, and since phi is surjective on k-points, im u_Z = im v_{Z'}.

The next page uses this to finish (iii). For (ii): if Z is tau-equivalent to 0, then m u = 0; divisibility of A_Y(k) forces u = 0. It then draws corollaries: algebraically trivial cycles are, modulo Albanese equivalence, exactly the classes Z(a) for homomorphic families over abelian varieties, and the group of algebraically trivial classes is divisible.

Purpose: to build a theory of 'Albanese equivalence' and 'intermediate Albanese' groups A^i_alb(X) as a tool for the standard conjectures and Hodge/Tate questions. The parametrization of algebraically trivial cycles by abelian varieties is the key structural input.
errors: The identity U(a) = nN holds only in A_{0,alb}(Y), not as cycles. Concluding Z(U(a)) = nZ(N) needs Z (equivalently u_Z) to respect Albanese equivalence on 0-cycles. This is implicit in u_Z being defined on A_{0,alb}(Y) = A_Y(k), but the page does not state it.

The bookkeeping of n is muddled: a crossed-out line gives n^2 Z(N), and the last displayed formula repeats 'Z'(S_y(N)) = n Z(N)' where the divisibility argument should yield Z'(S_Y(L)) = Z(N) with N = nL. The intended conclusion (n can be eliminated, i.e. one may take phi = n) is correct.

The existence of U with S_Y(U(a)) = na is asserted without proof. It is standard (curve section, Jacobian, Poincaré reducibility, Poincaré divisor), but one must normalize so that U(a) has degree 0 and U(0) is Albanese-trivial.

ideas.what: Quasi-universal family of 0-cycles: a cycle U on Y x Alb(Y) with S(U(a)) = n a, used instead of a non-existent universal family
ideas.modern_name: Quasi-section of the Albanese map via Jacobians of curves (isogeny trick, Poincaré reducibility)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil, Lang, Matsusaka (1950s theory of Albanese and Jacobian varieties)

ideas.what: Factoring a correspondence-induced map Alb(Y)(k) -> {cycles mod Albanese equivalence} through an algebraic homomorphic family over an abelian variety, up to isogeny, then removing the isogeny by divisibility
ideas.modern_name: Algebraically trivial cycles parametrized by abelian varieties; regular homomorphisms / algebraic representatives
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil, Samuel (adequate and Albanese-type equivalences), later Saito (1979) and Murre (1983-85) for algebraic representatives

ideas.what: Using divisibility of A_Y(k) to kill torsion obstructions (tau-equivalence implies the induced map is zero)
ideas.modern_name: Divisibility of the group of algebraically trivial cycles; torsion versus divisible argument

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine verification within Grothendieck's unpublished theory of Albanese equivalence: an isogeny trick plus divisibility to factor correspondences through abelian varieties. The page is mostly corrections of the n-bookkeeping. The results are standard (Weil–Lang–Samuel; later Murre's algebraic representatives), and nothing here appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The last displayed formula reads 'Z'(S_y(N)) = n Z(N)' with a short sign before Z that may be a sloppy 'n' or a dash; the intended conclusion after replacing N by L is Z'(S_Y(L)) = Z(N).
Final line probably reads 'Ceci permet aussi d'éliminer la multiplication par n' (or similar) rather than 'Ce qui permet d'éliminer'.
Marginal note after the formula Z'(S_y(N)) = n Z(N): 'N de degré 0 sur Y' — correct.
In the crossed-out block the bracketed insertion reads approximately 'de degré 0 de A_{0 alb}(Y) identifié à'; the subsequent 'de la forme nL (car A_Y(k) est divisible!)' refers to N.
